item_name: Circuit Board (Printed Circuit Board / PCB — Populated & Bare)
hazards: Lead-tin solder and brominated flame retardants (BFRs) in FR-4 fiberglass resin
Beryllium copper in edge connectors and sockets
Trace cadmium, chromium, and mercury in mounted ICs and switches
safe_handling: Hold circuit boards by the edges wearing gloves to avoid sharp solder pins and fiberglass splinters
Store upright or stacked neatly in dry, non-conductive bins
unsafe_actions: Never burn circuit boards in open air to melt solder
Never use unventilated acid baths to strip gold
Do not saw, drill, or sand FR-4 boards without dust extraction
what_to_do_if_damaged: If a board is snapped, cracked, or delaminated, wear gloves and a dust mask to avoid inhaling fiberglass dust, sweep fragments carefully, and seal them in a puncture-resistant container.
disposal_route: Channel directly to a CPCB-registered e-waste dismantler or precious-metal recycler; never sell to informal scrap dealers.
environmental_impact: Open burning and crude acid stripping of circuit boards are major sources of dioxin, furan, and heavy-metal contamination in air, soil, and groundwater.
